The halt came after 48h WR hit 29.8%, and the 24h data since confirms why it was right to halt: 43 closed trades, 15 wins (34.9%), -2.02 USDT. We were on the wrong side, not unlucky.

The single open trade is a BTC SHORT (ai-trader-manual, 10x, entry 81522, -0.11%, 3.7h). Regime alignment is mixed: 15m and 4h scanners both say SHORT_BIAS (aligned with the trade), but the 1m continuum shows BTC sitting AT the EMA300 (81578) with zscore +1.93 STRONG_POS and LEAN_BULL 15m/1h linreg — a squeeze is in progress against us. The trade thesis is intact though: BTC lower-highs from 82140 → 81700s → 81600s and the scanners see the downtrend. SL at 81766 is only 0.30% above current 81615 (tight, good), TP 80299 is 1.6% below (R:R ~1:5). HOLD the short — the tight SL caps the squeeze risk, and the position earns if the SHORT_BIAS structure resumes. If it stops out, that is the market telling us the bounce has more room, not that the short was wrong at entry.

The 24h bleeding was almost entirely LONGs into a short-bias market: 31 longs (-1.66) vs 12 shorts (-0.36). Aggregate regime scan right now: 44 tokens SHORT_BIAS vs 12 LONG_BIAS. We kept buying dumps and the dumps kept dumping.

Why weren't we on it? doji-bottom-long fires on a bullish reversal candle at the bottom of a dump — but in a SHORT_BIAS regime the 'bottom' is a rest stop, not a reversal. The doji is the market catching its breath before the next leg down. Long side = 40% WR; shorting the continuation was the trade.

2) doji-bottom-long DEATH STREAK — 5 consecutive losses, 10 trades/24h, 4W, -0.53 USDT. All five losers were longs into SHORT_BIAS or collapsing coins (ZEN 29.5, WCT 27.8, CRV 39.8, MET 47.6, YGG 48.8 RSI). The signal itself isn't broken in bull regimes — it's a chop-regime knife-catcher. It has no regime gate.
